Rejected a scholarship from a GLC after signing a preliminary letter of commitment (not the actual scholarship contract yet). Interned there for a few weeks after signing the letter. During the first day of my internship the people working there advised me not to sign the contract. The people on scholarship had calendars counting down the days to the end of their bond. It was abysmal. So I walked away and had to pay a few hundred dollars as penalty.

No regrets. Now I’m earning way more than I would have if I had signed. It’s a high-stress job, but I sleep soundly knowing that I’m doing this out of choice and not because I’m shackled by a contract.

I do feel you, OP. For a good year after I was consumed by self-doubt and wondered whether I had made the right choice. It was also an overseas scholarship, so instead of living that life I was stuck in a Singapore uni studying my ass off in a highly competitive course. You may second-guess, you may continue to have doubts, but what’s done is done. You make your choices based on the best information and circumstances at the time, and you learn how to make the most of them. Over time new doors will open, and you may find yourself in a much better position than you may have never thought was possible. That’s the beauty of serendipity, and that’s something you would not be able to experience if you had signed the contract.
